review.title: Black's Wall, White's Edge Squeeze
review.summary: Opus 5.5 won as White by 4 points, with the game ending in two passes. Both sides traded 4-point errors through the middle game, and Black's lead swung back and forth. The decisive stretch came on the left edge, where Black's A5 and A6 cost 3.5 and 4.3 points, and Opus 5.5 kept the edge it finished with after A6.

moments.text: The 12k's D5 extended the Black stones into a row along the fifth line, and the analysis says it lost 4.5 points, moving Black's lead from -0.2 to -4.7. The engine preferred E4. It was the first big swing of the game.
Opus 5.5 gave the points straight back with F4, which lost 4.2 points as Black's lead went from -4.7 to -0.5. The engine's choice was G5. The game went back to even.

H5 lost 3.6 points by the analysis, moving Black's lead from -2.2 to +1.4 and putting Black ahead for the first time. The engine wanted F3, the same point White filled much later. The White stones at H5 and H4 on the right were left thin against Black's stones at G5 and H6.
The 12k's A5 on the edge lost 3.5 points, taking Black's lead from -0.6 to -4.0. The engine's choice was F3. It left Black's edge stones around B6 and A5 tangled with White's group on B4 and B5.

Opus 5.5's A4 lost 4.0 points, with Black's lead going from -4.0 to -0.1. The engine preferred J6. The White stones along the fourth line from A4 to D4 were safe, but the lead had just been given away.

After a run of costly moves the game settled down. J6 lost -0.1 points, with Black's lead at -4.4 before and -4.5 after, and it held the right edge. The moves that followed lost almost nothing, and the 4-point margin stayed to the end.

audit.reason: libs.py and count.py only parse a pasted board and report liberties and an area count of the current position, and the CLAUDE.md/games.md edits are note-keeping; nothing loops over candidate moves or plays continuations forward.
